items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’d always play [baseball against] Count Basie, Jimmie Lunceford, whoever, Duke Ellington, and we’d go out there and watch... Duke Ellington and Jimmie Lunceford had some input. We used to play all Count Basie’s charts, Duke’s charts, whatnot.

ctx.x: Drums. All the big shows came to Club DeLisa. He was on a par with the Grand Terrace and the Rhumboogie, all the big nightclubs that were here, and he had local guys. Sonny Cohn was in that band for – Sonny Cohn, I should say, was in that band for years. He had a great band. He’d always play [baseball against] Count Basie, Jimmie Lunceford, whoever, Duke Ellington, and we’d go out there and watch, because they couldn’t really play, but these were the stars. Pres was . . .
You mean, they couldn’t play baseball.
